Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Rejections commonly result from missing priority and ship_country; qty was also missing in the Cy Reyes attempts.
- Do not infer or fabricate missing values. Extract values from the complete source record, preserving customer, email, and date accurately.
- Source excerpts may be truncated in the displayed prompt; avoid treating incomplete text as complete data. If required fields cannot be verified, leave them missing rather than guessing.
- A corrected resubmission can be accepted on attempt 2: Bo Okafor and Dee Reyes succeeded after initial rejection. Eli Okafor also succeeded on attempt 2.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 demonstrated this.
- Handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, and partner-portal origins do not by themselves determine validity; completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- For each submission, ensure all six required keys are present and correctly named (especially “priority,” not “prio”), with valid values before submitting.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six correctly named keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Rejections commonly involve missing/invalid priority and ship_country; qty can also be missing or invalid (as in ORD-5118/5119).
- Extract only from a complete, verifiable source record. Displayed excerpts may be truncated; never treat partial text as complete or infer/fabricate values. If any required field cannot be verified, leave it missing and do not submit.
- Preserve customer, email, date, quantity, country, and priority accurately. Intake annotations such as “ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” or customer confirmation do not supply/validate other missing fields.
- Origin (voicemail, transcription, phone, email, handwritten, or partner portal) does not determine validity; completeness and accurate mapping do.
- Track attempts per order, including across repeated intake batches. Corrected resubmissions can succeed on attempt 2 (Bo Okafor, Dee Reyes, Eli Okafor), but only after all six fields are verified.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 and ORD-5110–5117 demonstrate this. Do not continue submitting after attempt 3.
- Recent records ORD-5110–5117 repeatedly failed because truncated sources left priority and ship_country unverifiable. ORD-5118/5119 also lacked qty; avoid repeating submissions without a complete source.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six correctly named keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Every required value must come from a complete, verifiable source record. Truncated excerpts such as “deliv,” “deliver_,” or “prio” do not verify delivery country or priority. Never infer, fabricate, or submit incomplete data.
- Rejections frequently involve missing/invalid priority and ship_country; qty may also be missing or invalid. Recent ORD-5121–5129 confirm that partial sources can produce repeated failures across attempts, even when customer, email, date, and quantity are visible.
- Intake annotations (“ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” customer confirmation, transcription status, or source origin) do not validate or replace missing fields. Origin does not determine validity.
- Preserve all six values accurately and map source names correctly (e.g., client → cust, contact → email, units_ordered → qty), but submit only when every field is independently verifiable.
- Track attempts per order, including repeated batches/resubmissions. Corrected resubmissions may succeed on attempt 2, but only after complete verification.
- Three failed attempts send the order to manual review; do not submit again after attempt 3. ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, and ORD-5129 reached manual review.
- If a source is truncated or any required field is uncertain, stop and await/obtain the complete source rather than guessing or using annotations.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six correctly named keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Map source names accurately (account_holder → cust, e_mail → email, ordered_on → order_date, count → qty, ship_to_country → ship_country). Preserve values exactly.
- Submit only when every required value is present in a complete, independently verifiable source record. Truncated excerpts (“pri,” “prior,” “deliv,” “ship_to_”) do not verify priority, quantity, or shipping country.
- Never infer, fabricate, normalize from context, or rely on intake annotations such as “ordinary priority,” duplicate-check claims, customer confirmation, transcription status, partner-portal origin, or handwritten-source claims. Annotations do not validate or replace fields.
- The most frequent failures remain priority and ship_country; qty can also be absent/invalid. ORD-5130–5139 confirm that repeated partial sources cause rejection, including cases where customer, email, date, and sometimes quantity are visible.
- Output must contain only the six required fields. Do not submit explanatory objects, status/error fields, or placeholders; “awaiting complete source” is an internal decision, not a valid intake submission.
- Track attempts per order, including repeated batches/resubmissions. A corrected resubmission may succeed only after complete verification.
- Three failed attempts send the order to manual review. Do not submit again on attempt 3; if required data is still uncertain, stop rather than guess.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly these six correctly named keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Map source names exactly: account_holder → cust, e_mail → email, ordered_on → order_date, count → qty, ship_to_country → ship_country. Preserve values exactly.
- Submit only when every required value is present in a complete, independently verifiable source record. Truncated excerpts (“pri,” “prior,” “deliv,” “ship_to_”) do not verify fields.
- Never infer, fabricate, normalize from context, or rely on annotations such as ordinary priority, duplicate-check claims, customer confirmations, transcription status, phone/front-desk handling, emailed origin, or handwritten-source claims. These do not validate or replace fields.
- Repeated partial records remain invalid even when customer, email, date, and sometimes quantity are visible. Priority and ship_country are frequent failures; qty may also be missing or invalid.
- Output only the six required fields. Never include explanations, status/error fields, or placeholders. “Awaiting complete source” is an internal decision, not a submission.
- Track attempts per order, including repeated batches/resubmissions. A corrected resubmission may succeed only after complete verification.
- On attempt 3, do not submit unless all six fields are independently verified. If any required value remains uncertain, stop; the order goes to manual review. Three failed attempts exhaust the allowance.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six correctly named keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use priority, never prio.
- Exact source-name mapping: account_holder → cust, e_mail → email, ordered_on → order_date, count → qty, ship_to_country → ship_country. Preserve values exactly.
- Submit only when every field is present and independently verifiable in one complete source record. Truncated excerpts or keys (e.g., “pri,” “prior,” “ship_to_”) do not verify values.
- Never infer, fabricate, normalize, or substitute from context. Front-desk statements, duplicate-check claims, “ordinary priority,” customer confirmations, transcription/handwritten/voicemail claims, phone handling, emailed or portal origin, and similar annotations do not validate or replace missing fields.
- Repeated partial records remain invalid. Recent failures confirm that visible customer, email, and date do not justify submission when priority, ship_country, or qty is missing/uncertain.
- Track attempts per order, including repeated batches and resubmissions. A corrected resubmission may succeed only after complete verification.
- On attempt 3, submit only if all six fields are independently verified. Otherwise stop and send to manual review; do not submit an empty or partial object. Three failed attempts exhaust the allowance.
- Output only the six required fields. Never include explanations, status/error fields, placeholders, or “awaiting complete source”; those are internal decisions.
